title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee’s 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to promote responsible AI use. It calls for greater transparency, accountability, and public engagement, and lays out a roadmap for implementing the report’s recommendations.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining its plan to oversee how artificial intelligence is used in educational qualifications, ensuring fairness, reliability and transparency. The guidance aims to help exam bodies and educators comply with new rules that safeguard the integrity of assessment processes while encouraging responsible AI innovation.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used in training and developing artificial intelligence systems, evaluating the legal and ethical implications of such use. It offers recommendations to balance the protection of creators’ rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government answered the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, saying the UK cannot afford to be complacent about artificial intelligence. It lays out plans to boost responsible AI research, put safeguards in place to manage risks, and ensure the benefits of AI are shared widely.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference and provides FAQs for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It defines the committee’s scope, responsibilities, and the key questions it will explore to ensure AI aligns with public expectations and regulations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines their perspective on how AI should be regulated and managed within the UK.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy outlines how AI technology will influence the regulation of medical products, ensuring safety, efficacy, and compliance. It applies the AI White Paper principles to guide the development, approval, and oversight of AI‑enabled medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a plan to make our defence forces the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential users of AI in the world for a country of our size. It focuses on leveraging AI technologies to enhance operations, decision‑making and global standing while upholding strong ethical and trust standards.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to use AI to improve services and operations, while carefully handling potential risks. It sets out strategies and measures to ensure that AI is adopted safely, responsibly, and in a way that benefits passengers, workers and the wider economy.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report tracks how copyright‑protected content is being used in training AI models, evaluating compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act's Section 137. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommendations for aligning AI development with copyright law.
